import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 1093

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/1093](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1093)
-/

namespace Erdos1093

open Finset Nat

/--
If defined, the deficiency is the count of $0 \le i < k$ such that $n - i$ is $k$-smooth.
-/
noncomputable def deficiency (n k : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  #{i ∈ range k | n - i ∈ smoothNumbers k}

/--
Are there infinitely many binomial coefficients with deficiency 1?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_1093.parts.i :
    answer(sorry) ↔ {x : ℕ × ℕ | let k := x.1; let n := x.2; 2 * k ≤ n ∧ deficiency n k = 1 ∧
      ∀ p, p.Prime → (p ∣ choose n k) → k < p}.Infinite := by
  sorry

/--
Are there only finitely many binomial coefficients with deficiency > 1?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_1093.parts.ii :
    {x : ℕ × ℕ | let k := x.1; let n := x.2; 2 * k ≤ n ∧ deficiency n k > 1 ∧
      ∀ p, p.Prime → (p ∣ choose n k) → k < p}.Finite := by
  sorry

end Erdos1093

findings.description: The membership test `n - i ∈ smoothNumbers k` counts numbers whose prime factors are strictly less than k, whereas the source requires prime factors at most k. This changes the deficiency even on the admissible domain. For example, n = 7 and k = 3 satisfy 2*k ≤ n, and choose 7 3 = 35 has all prime factors greater than 3. The source deficiency is 1 because 6 is the unique qualifying number among 7, 6, 5, but the Lean definition returns 0. These facts were kernel-checked in Lean. This incorrect count is used by both problem statements.
findings.source_evidence: https://www.erdosproblems.com/1093 explicitly defines k-smooth here as “divisible only by primes ≤ k” and lists binom(7,3) as having deficiency 1. The original ELS88 paper, p.522, likewise counts the terms with b_i = 1 after separating prime factors ≤ k from those > k: https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1988-26.pdf.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace `smoothNumbers k` with `smoothNumbers (k + 1)`: `noncomputable def deficiency (n k : ℕ) : ℕ := #{i ∈ range k | n - i ∈ smoothNumbers (k + 1)}`. Clarify in the docstring that the prime factors are at most k. This correction reproduces all 23 examples displayed on the source page.

reformulations.difference: Uses infinitude of admissible parameter pairs rather than infinitude of distinct numerical binomial coefficients. This representation choice is separate from the deficiency-threshold defect.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Holding the deficiency predicate fixed, positive deficiency excludes k = 0. For 1 ≤ k and 2*k ≤ n, n ≤ choose n k. Consequently, every pair representing a fixed coefficient C satisfies k ≤ C and n ≤ C, so the coefficient map has finite fibers on the admissible set. The pair set is infinite exactly when its image under (k,n) ↦ choose n k is infinite. This equivalence was proved in the scratch file.

reformulations.difference: Uses finiteness of admissible parameter pairs rather than finiteness of distinct numerical binomial coefficients. This representation choice is separate from the deficiency-threshold defect.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The condition deficiency > 1 excludes k = 0. Together with 2*k ≤ n, this gives n ≤ choose n k. Each coefficient C therefore has only finitely many admissible representations, all within k,n ≤ C. A finite image consequently has a finite pair set, and the converse follows because images of finite sets are finite. The equivalence was proved in Lean.

review.notes: Checked all three declarations. No additional independent defect was found. Both theorem domains correctly impose the conditions under which deficiency is defined; totalizing the helper outside that domain is harmless. The k=0 and k=1 boundaries add no qualifying pairs, and the bound prevents truncated-subtraction or zero-binomial issues. The source still records both questions as open; conditional and computational progress in its comments does not contradict the tags. Final checks compile successfully in /workspace/review/scratch.lean, including kernel-checked counterexamples, all displayed source examples, and the pair/value equivalences. ELS93's full text was unavailable; the cited website and ELS88 directly establish the definition and problem needed for this review. The target file was not modified.

submission.summary: Changed the cutoff to `smoothNumbers (k + 1)` and clarified that prime factors may equal k. The requested compilation succeeds with only `sorry` warnings. Kernel-checked regression tests confirm deficiency(7,3) = 1 and deficiency(47,11) = 4.

namespace Erdos1093

open Finset Nat

/--
If defined, the deficiency is the count of $0 \le i < k$ such that $n - i$ is $k$-smooth,

-/

  #{i ∈ range k | n - i ∈ smoothNumbers (k + 1)}

/--

-/

    answer(sorry) ↔ {x : ℕ × ℕ | let k := x.1; let n := x.2; 2 * k ≤ n ∧ deficiency n k = 1 ∧
      ∀ p, p.Prime → (p ∣ choose n k) → k < p}.Infinite := by
  sorry

/--
Are there only finitely many binomial coefficients with deficiency > 1?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_1093.parts.ii :
    {x : ℕ × ℕ | let k := x.1; let n := x.2; 2 * k ≤ n ∧ deficiency n k > 1 ∧
      ∀ p, p.Prime → (p ∣ choose n k) → k < p}.Finite := by
  sorry

end Erdos1093
